Answer: B
Reason: In an HIV-positive patient, the combination of right upper lobe consolidation and ill-defined basal shadowing is characteristic of Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome, where migrating larvae cause transient pulmonary infiltrates and alveolar hemorrhage alongside bacterial superinfection. This specific radiographic pattern in this clinical context distinguishes it from typical presentations of PCP (usually bilateral diffuse interstitial disease) or miliary TB (diffuse micronodules).
